newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end up, buoyed by plantation sale.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end up, buoyed by plantation sale.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on positive sentiment after a controlling stake in a plantation firm sailed through the stock exchange at a premium on Friday, brokers said.
A 51 percent holding in Maturata Plantations Ltd, introduced at a minimum price of 30 rupees a share, was bought by the Employees Trust Fund, a state managed gratuity fund, brokers said.
"It shows the value the market has placed on our plantations," said a trader at Somerville Stockbrokers, who made the successful bid.

The sale of Maturata was part of the government's privatisation process where it is selling controlling interest through the stock exchange. Two more plantations will be privatised next week by selling 51 percent.
The all share closed 3.1 points up at 731.9 on a turnover of 30.2 million rupees. Blue chips Hayley and Aitken Spence gained 4.75 each to 234.75 rupees and 159.75 rupees.
Brokers said retailers were coming into the market, buoyed by prospects in the plantation sector.
"Institutions are interested in blue chips, but they can't find volume," said Hiran Seneviratne of Lanka Securities.
